scope: Independent skeptical source review of inherited P0/P1 findings; source-level evidence, not live incident frequency

verdicts.evidence: turn_events.ex:9-10 calls port_metadata on each event; turn_loop.ex:156 calls it in the notification path; app_server_port.ex:212-218 invokes process_group_for_pid; remote_control.ex:283-294 and 448-466 run ps with retries. This is synchronous work in a streamed hot path.
verdicts.limitations: The per-turn delta count and observed CPU/latency cost were not measured; the remote worker-host assertion needs separate route-specific confirmation.

verdicts.evidence: claude/config.ex:33-37 maps every unrecognized permission_mode to bypassPermissions, while config/schema/agent.ex:76-83 casts an unrestricted string and Claude.Config.validate! checks only command. A typo in a configured stricter value changes effective permission policy.
verdicts.limitations: Default bypassPermissions is intentional in this revision; this finding concerns a configured invalid value, not the default itself.

verdicts.evidence: display_tailer.ex:322-325 truncates at max_body bytes with binary_part, then forwards the resulting body and output at 290-295. A multibyte codepoint straddling the byte boundary yields invalid UTF-8. issue_log.ex:993-1009 documents the same previously fixed failure at a different boundary.
verdicts.limitations: The exact downstream database and channel failure paths were source-traced, not reproduced with a live socket; the truncation defect itself is deterministic.

verdicts.evidence: claude/coding_agent.ex:143-159 checks only expanded path prefix; codex/app_server_port.ex:12-38 canonicalizes both paths and detects symlink escape. Claude stop_port at 443-462 merely closes the port whereas Codex at 144-172 reaps descendants first. These are concrete safety divergence examples, not just similar code.
verdicts.limitations: The broad claim that all duplicated session plumbing should become one abstraction is a design recommendation; affected Claude deployment prevalence is unmeasured.

verdicts.evidence: claude/remote_control.ex houses process-group and kill helpers and is imported by codex/app_server_port.ex:141,158 and app_server/adapter.ex:253. The ownership and dependency direction are as claimed.
verdicts.limitations: Naming/package placement alone does not establish a P1 runtime failure. The proposed split needs caller and lifecycle contracts before implementation.

verdicts.evidence: codex/dynamic_tool.ex:1-26 hosts common tool dispatch; its LinearGraphQL and ReviewThreads handlers default directly to LinearClient.graphql and GitHubClient review mutations, while Claude imports the common tool surface. This is a real package ownership conflict.
verdicts.limitations: A misplaced shared surface is architectural debt; the evidence does not show a P1 operational defect or quantify the claimed 1,400 lines as removable.

verdicts.evidence: notification_policy.ex:36-53 falls back to payload_text for every map; lines 184-195 recursively include both map keys and values. repl/hook_turn.ex:115-122 passes the entire stop_failure event.raw, so unrelated path or message text can contain a limit marker.
verdicts.limitations: Actual misclassification frequency is unknown, and individual transcript records may have a narrower shape than the raw hook event.

verdicts.evidence: remote_control.ex:73-86 reads and rewrites all of ~/.claude.json via Fs.atomic_write without preservation options. fs.ex:19-52 uses a temporary file and rename but contains no backup, cross-process lock or original-mode transfer. The documentation's backup-guarded guarantee is contradicted by the implementation.
verdicts.limitations: No concurrent-write incident or original file mode was observed; loss and mode change are reachable races/conditions, not measured rates.

verdicts.evidence: chat_completions.ex:39-56 routes valid models into marker handling without authorization; 131-149 forwards coalesced text before stream. operator_dispatch.ex:17-25 checks Caller.authorize only in the ordinary text branch. Bridge has no outer auth plug.
verdicts.limitations: Loopback exposure is deployment-dependent; a reachable local agent process suffices. A newer Muse branch is outside this frozen verdict.

verdicts.evidence: command_runner.ex:10 names GITHUB_TOKEN and GH_TOKEN for inheritance; 80-99 copies nonempty daemon values after clearenv; 207-215 drops scrub/unset entries. This directly violates the stated raw-token isolation contract.
verdicts.limitations: The claim requires one token in daemon environment; deployment may supply a credential file instead, but the supported dotenv path does populate it.

verdicts.evidence: session_writer.ex:190-202 and 221-255 suppress SQL writes when live_stream_active?; 261-267 defines that only as ActiveTurns IDs, not bridge subscriber presence. TurnStream closure can therefore leave an active turn with no sink.
verdicts.limitations: Window frequency and precise event loss were not measured in a live chat pane; the state predicate is demonstrably insufficient.

verdicts.evidence: attach_pool.ex:899-916, hidden_window.ex:104-120 and slot/attach_pane.ex:48-62 hard-code aiur-orangekid-default and swallow command failures. Other users and instance keys cannot hit that target.
verdicts.limitations: AttachPool.ensure_hidden_geometry may be dead; the other call sites establish a current resize defect. Claimed 5-7 second cost was not measured here.

verdicts.evidence: sensitive_responses.ex:87-100 falls back to retained_for_port? for any unmatched binary and does not remove retained IDs; await.ex:34-36 retains a timed-out sensitive request. This can suppress later malformed lines until cleanup.
verdicts.limitations: The downstream quota-misclassification consequence requires a qualifying provider banner and was not reproduced; severity is lower than the inherited P1 absent occurrence evidence.

verdicts.evidence: attach_pool.ex:106-110 uses the 5-second GenServer.call default and converts exits to :miss; handle_call at 203-208 enters synchronous consume_via_slot, which invokes Slot.set_visible. Other readers have 1-second calls and fallback values.
verdicts.limitations: A concrete slow slot move is required; the claimed duplicate pane and stale mailbox reply were source-inferred, not witnessed.

verdicts.evidence: slot.ex:192-198, 213-229 and 403-405 keep the Slot process alive with status :failed; no restart follows from a supervisor while the child remains alive. The documented restart behavior is therefore false.
verdicts.limitations: An actual boot or serve failure is required. Recovery may occur through an external restart not represented in these state transitions.

verdicts.evidence: slot_policy.ex:236-270 has no termination handler; grow_slot at 303-320 increments highest_started and keeps live_slots, and start_slots at 376-393 uses next_missing_slot. A dead registered slot is not removed from policy state.
verdicts.limitations: A supervisor restart with the same slot index may mask some failures; the policy itself does not reconcile the count.

verdicts.evidence: db.ex:66-78 commits regardless of a returned {:error, reason} and discards COMMIT result. session_writer.ex:352-355 discards root insert result, and replay_events at 404-412 counts only successes. Transaction reporting can therefore contradict persistence.
verdicts.limitations: The exact SQLite error condition was not induced; the control-flow defect is visible without one.

verdicts.evidence: tool_call_ledger.ex:43-51 loads all durable entries; 109-126 writes a running entry on claim and the completion path retains done result. No retention or deletion path was found in the module, so memory and store grow with lifetime calls.
verdicts.limitations: The 2 GB DETS endpoint and fsync throughput were not measured; classify these as predicted consequences, not observed impact.

verdicts.evidence: active_turns.ex:171-176 and token_registry.ex ensure_table create named public ETS tables in whichever process calls first. An owner restart followed by a short-lived caller can erase fresh tokens/turn state; concurrent creation can race.
verdicts.limitations: The initial supervised boot path may normally make the intended owner first. This concerns restart/race windows, not ordinary steady state.

verdicts.evidence: QueueDrain paused branches and pause-agent receives omit PauseContainment.confirm while TurnLoop confirms; the containment fallback is armed for paused Codex sessions. The five-second timer can reap a deliberately paused process group.
verdicts.limitations: Applies to the queue-drain pause paths, not every pause; exact timer execution was not reproduced.

verdicts.evidence: QueueDrain hard-matches :ok on fallible Orchestrator restore/consume calls; TurnLoop explicitly uses best-effort bookkeeping for these replies. A transient {:error, :unavailable} becomes a MatchError on queue turns.
verdicts.limitations: How often the Orchestrator returns the transient error is not measured.

verdicts.evidence: turn_loop.ex:83-225 and queue_drain.ex:618-791 implement parallel turn pipelines; the missing containment confirmation and differing queue error handling are concrete divergent safety behavior.
verdicts.limitations: Sharing the whole pipeline is a design choice; this verdict confirms the drift, not a particular extraction strategy.

verdicts.evidence: claude/repl/operator_inject.ex:74-87 invokes on_failure after send failure without checking its result; CheckpointDelivery callback restores queue state through a fallible Orchestrator call. If restore fails, delivered state can survive to the normal consume sweep.
verdicts.limitations: Requires both send failure and restore failure; no live frequency or replay outcome was observed.

verdicts.evidence: ToolExecutor chooses issue.id before issue.identifier for coordination keys, while bootstrap_digest.ex:53-55 and the runner use identifier. A tracker whose opaque id differs from its visible identifier can route tool events to another key.
verdicts.limitations: GitHub id and identifier coincide in the cited normalizer, so impact is confined to trackers with distinct IDs.

verdicts.evidence: Tmux.Protocol is a control-mode parser but production Tmux shells out per command and has no producer for {:tmux_event, _}; PaneManager subscription cannot receive pane-died in ordinary operation.
verdicts.limitations: Lazy pane reconciliation may limit user impact; dead code alone is below P1 severity.

verdicts.evidence: agent_list/input.ex:110-111 sends ? to help toggle and q unconditionally to App.quit; the overlay text says q leaves help. App.quit enters full shutdown, so the displayed instruction can stop the daemon.
verdicts.limitations: The user must follow the help instruction; whether a launcher restarts after shutdown is deployment-dependent.

verdicts.evidence: bootstrap_digest.ex:140 onward logs and returns :ok after enqueue failure, and CommentContext converts fetch failures to empty collections. First-turn context can omit missed events/review comments without retry.
verdicts.limitations: A later poll or operator message may eventually deliver some information; permanent loss is not established for every event.

verdicts.evidence: Generic AgentRunner references Codex/Claude-specific modules and Orchestrator internals directly. This is a real dependency direction obstacle for package extraction.
verdicts.limitations: The source claim is architectural; it does not demonstrate a P1 production defect.

verdicts.evidence: ticket_detail_coordinator.ex:145-153 refreshes any nonfresh, noninflight entry; policy.ex:73-77 deems failures nonfresh. Failure completion broadcasts and the open LiveView requests again, closing an unbacked feedback loop.
verdicts.limitations: Requires an open drawer and a persistent failed read; call rate was not measured.

verdicts.evidence: ticket_detail_sanitizer.ex:158-169 rejects body byte_size over limit before sanitizing; the normalizer propagates that error to the whole detail snapshot, with an effective 16 KiB cap.
verdicts.limitations: The prevalence of >16 KiB issue bodies is uncounted; the claim is conditional on one.

verdicts.evidence: graph_projection.ex:318-329 ignores the reconciliation result but stamps last_reconciliation_ms; 341-349 also clears crashed task state without retry. A failed boot reconciliation is therefore treated as complete until another trigger.
verdicts.limitations: Delivery-mode and later refresh triggers determine duration of staleness; absence of all recovery is configuration-dependent.

verdicts.evidence: github_graph/reconciliation.ex:66-72 clears every sub_issue edge before redeposit; queries.ex:38-40 explicitly acknowledges first-100 member limit. Membership beyond page one can disappear at each reconciliation.
verdicts.limitations: Requires a root with >100 members or invalid connection; actual current root population should be counted before sizing remediation.

verdicts.evidence: catalog_store.ex:118 onward explicitly mirrors GitHubGraph.Normalizer; its first-100 member cap differs from normalizer treatment of incomplete connections. Shared metric rules have diverged.
verdicts.limitations: The affected >100-member population is not counted, so P1 impact is not established by duplication alone.

verdicts.evidence: planning_source.ex:872-875 accepts github.number while pack_status.ex:372-373 recognizes only ticket. Equivalent manifest ticket references can receive different materialization/status treatment.
verdicts.limitations: Need a census of real manifests using github.number alone before calling this P1.

verdicts.evidence: graph_projection_policy.ex:185 maps :auth and :forbidden, but github/errors.ex:137-139 emits :permission for ordinary 403. The fallback labels a permission failure as provider unavailable.
verdicts.limitations: This is a misleading diagnostic with potentially material troubleshooting cost, but no P1 outage follows from the classifier alone.

verdicts.evidence: graph_projection.ex:823-829 computes member_labels? and passes reader options, while the configured CatalogStore reader ignores that flag. The separate label-read cadence has no effect on its reads.
verdicts.limitations: Dead machinery is a deletion candidate; no P1 runtime regression is shown. Verify alternate reader injection before removing.

verdicts.evidence: graph_projection.ex is 1,825 lines with catalog, selected scopes, reconciliation and subscriptions in one GenServer; Options constructs a wide state map. The responsibility count is supportable from source.
verdicts.limitations: Size and cohesion are maintainability findings, not P1 failures; extracting modules should retain atomic projection behavior.

verdicts.evidence: graph_projection.ex:381-389 reschedules through reconcile before request_scope; request_scope defers at max_inflight (794-795) while due retry state can re-arm a 0 ms timer. The control flow permits repeated immediate messages under saturation.
verdicts.limitations: Static trace only; a bounded scheduler reproduction is still needed to establish rate and CPU impact.

verdicts.evidence: graph_projection.ex:1513-1525 rescues subscription failures as :ok; options.ex:193-199 suppresses resource subscription failure. No retry is visible, so an event-sourced projection can miss all future resource changes after boot race.
verdicts.limitations: Requires subscription failure at startup; supervisor ordering may make it rare.

verdicts.evidence: AdHocSource and OpenTicketSource duplicate overlay lifecycle functions; ad_hoc_source.ex:274-282 follows unlimited Link pages, while OpenTicketSource caps them. The paging difference is concrete.
verdicts.limitations: The uncontrolled page count depends on real labelled issue volume; no P1 measured cost is supplied.

verdicts.evidence: github/issues.ex imports BuildOrder.Bounded for repository validation, demonstrating upward dependency from GitHub infrastructure into the proposed Build Order boundary; other cited imports show the same pattern.
verdicts.limitations: Dependency direction is planning-relevant, not a P1 operational defect.

verdicts.evidence: subscription_store.ex:375-393 drops IDs at/below cursor; retry_stalled at 398 onward resolves by re-sending buffered events to its own mailbox. Newer already-queued messages precede those sends and can move the cursor, silently discarding buffered events.
verdicts.limitations: Requires a transient stall and a newer event already queued; no live event-loss count was measured.

verdicts.evidence: claims.ex:256-260 permits B to claim when A is expired; do_renew at 265 onward touches A by ID without checking that a newer owner exists. Two live owner roles can result.
verdicts.limitations: Requires A to renew after lease lapse and B takeover; effect on actual acknowledgement order should be covered by a state test.

verdicts.evidence: github_ci_poller.ex:23-33 fans targets with 60-second task deadlines; the Orchestrator lifecycle calls poll synchronously. Slow GitHub calls can block the one Orchestrator mailbox.
verdicts.limitations: Fleet size and actual poll duration were not measured; worst-case formula is a bound, not an observed stall.

verdicts.evidence: delivery_mode.ex:218-225 emits never_delivered for configured_unproven with any activity and zero deliveries, without comparing threshold_ms. mode_registry.ex:186-196 resets observed activity on restart.
verdicts.limitations: False alert needs a newly observed activity before a delivery; a post-restart delivery before sweep avoids it.

verdicts.evidence: github_webhook/normalizer.ex:579-589 states REST webhook PR context lacks reviewDecision/head date and emits nil; github_comments_poller.ex:487-495 supplies them only from GraphQL. First-publisher dedup can make rework routing depend on arrival order.
verdicts.limitations: The word always is too broad if a future payload carries fields; current source path and webhook-shaped REST payload support the conditional defect.

verdicts.evidence: events/publisher.ex:41-46 imports GitHub.Config, AgentMarker, ResourceStore and Webhooks, then calls Webhooks.record_activity at 171-179; SubscriptionStore reaches Orchestrator. The proposed generic Events boundary has upward dependencies.
verdicts.limitations: Architectural blocker, not a demonstrated P1 failure.

verdicts.evidence: code_owners.ex:36-42 promises preserving previous allowlist, but do_refresh at 181-191 rebuilds allowlist from fresh resolution; failed team expansion returns empty. Trusted team members can disappear on refresh.
verdicts.limitations: Revocation of already-running agents depends on dispatch policy and active-state reevaluation; source path supports it but incident frequency is unknown.

verdicts.evidence: github/config.ex:604-612 converts missing or timed-out CodeOwners GenServer into []; code_owners.ex:110-112 serves snapshot synchronously. A slow refresh can make unknown trust look like explicit denial.
verdicts.limitations: Requires allowed_users fallback to CODEOWNERS and a busy or absent server.

verdicts.evidence: budget_map.ex:291-301 reports unavailable when glob finds no agent-cache files; its default glob omits match_dot while the runtime directory is hidden. Parser at 455 onward assumes a narrower row shape than the writer.
verdicts.limitations: The glob claim was not exercised in this review environment; regardless, this is a diagnostic panel defect rather than P1 dispatch risk.

verdicts.evidence: github/comments.ex:124-134 makes one per_page=100 read via fetch_json_list, whereas fetch_issue_comments_conditional at 89 onward uses its pagination-aware path. For oldest-first issues comments, comments beyond 100 are absent from classified context.
verdicts.limitations: Requires >100 issue/PR conversation comments; current ticket prevalence was not counted.

verdicts.evidence: github/config.ex:841 onward documents hardened pgrep parsing; claude/remote_control.ex:427-436 still String.to_integer parses stderr-merged pgrep output and can raise on nonnumeric output.
verdicts.limitations: A pgrep success status with malformed output is required; duplicate process-tree code itself is maintainability debt.

verdicts.evidence: github/client.ex:6 aliases BuildOrder.GitHubGraph and ProviderResult; 89-97 delegates catalog and selected-root reads back into Build Order, establishing a package cycle with GitHub transport.
verdicts.limitations: The count of unused delegates needs whole-repo call analysis; cycle alone is planning debt, not a P1 runtime defect.

verdicts.evidence: CodeOwners.parse_codeowners token validation treats inline comment tokens as malformed, while Aiur.Codeowners strips trailing # comments. The same CODEOWNERS text can therefore classify comments but collapse dispatch allowlist to trusted accounts.
verdicts.limitations: Affected repository CODEOWNERS syntax should be counted; if no inline comments, impact is latent.

verdicts.evidence: github/config.ex:413-417 preserves input case while 446-451 explicitly validates bot suffix case-insensitively; BotIdentity and Codeowners agent_login? use different comparisons.
verdicts.limitations: The exact 11-site count is not independently recounted; operational effect needs a mixed-case configured login.

verdicts.evidence: github/resource_store.ex:1-254 owns lifecycle and checkpoint contract; 295 onward defines consumer resource types in one shared module. It is a broad mutable cross-package boundary.
verdicts.limitations: Size and coupling are confirmed architectural concerns but not a P1 defect by themselves; do not treat line count as removable LOC.

verdicts.evidence: github/issues.ex:296-305 checks regression before put; resource_fetch.ex:206-216 writes directly. The store supports atomic update, but several order-sensitive writers bypass it, allowing a newer webhook value to be overwritten as fresh.
verdicts.limitations: Requires overlapping reads/writes to the same key; the five-writer and three-policy counts need a full caller census.

verdicts.evidence: github/review_threads/reply.ex:55 onward retries an addPullRequestReviewThreadReply mutation after retryable error. A timeout or 5xx can mean the mutation succeeded but the response was lost, so retry can duplicate it.
verdicts.limitations: No idempotency key is available in the cited path; exact GitHub ambiguous-failure frequency is unknown.

verdicts.evidence: github/quota.ex:136-140 makes preflight a synchronous 5-second call and catches exit as :ok. Heavy filesystem snapshot/alert work shares that GenServer, so a queued timeout fails budget admission open.
verdicts.limitations: The precise max snapshot duration and request rate need measurement; the fail-open branch makes the risk concrete.

verdicts.evidence: quota.ex:1234-1244 classifies GraphQL direction by a leading mutation regex, while other listed modules use different recognizers. Cost and attribution labels can diverge for the same request.
verdicts.limitations: The individual examples should be verified against actual production queries before severity exceeds P2.

verdicts.evidence: github/transport.ex:466-474 knows the Orchestrator process; github/quota.ex:36-45 imports Workspace.Layout and other nontransport state. Together with Client/BuildOrder references this blocks a clean GitHub package boundary.
verdicts.limitations: Architectural coupling, not directly a P1 operator-visible defect.

verdicts.evidence: decision_store.ex is 4,826 lines and combines durable event writer, projection repair, command lifecycle, delivery, dispatch scheduling and alerts in one GenServer. These responsibilities have different change reasons.
verdicts.limitations: Size alone is not P1; extraction must preserve persist-before-notify ordering.

verdicts.evidence: decision_store.ex:4365-4368 sets writable?: false on lifecycle append failure with Logger.error only; dispatch reads blocked_ticket_ids and fails closed when store health is unreadable. No in-process recovery branch was found.
verdicts.limitations: A durable append failure is required; restart recovery is available but operator visibility is poor without debug.

verdicts.evidence: decision_store.ex:733-764 treats derived projection write failure as store read-only. Mutations append first and some publication paths test next_state.writable?, so durable accepted events can remain unannounced.
verdicts.limitations: Exact caller path matters for each lifecycle event; the broad every-event wording should not be inferred.

verdicts.evidence: decision_store.ex:3256-3261 directly calls Tracker and Orchestrator.DispatchPolicy from a default terminal resolver, confirming upward dependency from decisions state to tracking/dispatch.
verdicts.limitations: This obstructs a proposed package boundary but is not itself a P1 runtime failure.

verdicts.evidence: commands_cli.ex:4-5 imports AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter.DecisionProvider and calls it at 107-113. The core CLI currently requires a web presenter dependency.
verdicts.limitations: The cited 15 other core imports were not individually counted in this verdict; architectural coupling is P2.

verdicts.evidence: agent_control_cli.ex is 3,408 lines, imports numerous independent subsystems and renders many distinct control commands. The source supports the responsibility concentration.
verdicts.limitations: Neither module length nor number of commands alone establishes a P1 failure.

verdicts.evidence: agent_control_cli.ex:187 onward prints several subsystem statuses serially after fleet sample; multiple GenServer reads have independent timeouts and BuildGate/Asks work can exceed launcher response budget.
verdicts.limitations: The sum of worst cases is a bound; typical latency and exact 10-second cut behavior require execution evidence.

verdicts.evidence: build_gate.ex:152 onward runs lock scans; 227 onward invokes external python without a bounded call. Dispatch admission synchronously reads this status in the Orchestrator process, so a hung scan can block its mailbox.
verdicts.limitations: Only when BuildGate is enabled and status reaches that path; no observed hang duration supplied.

verdicts.evidence: executor_events.ex:454 onward maps any JsonStore.read failure to empty subscribed_to/cursor; subscribe at 77-82 writes the derived state back. A transient unreadable file can be overwritten, and writers have no shared transaction.
verdicts.limitations: Requires read failure or overlapping writers; subscription-loss frequency is unknown.

verdicts.evidence: executor_events.ex:38-55 dedupes deferred events by searching journal; ensure_requested at 342-349 does likewise. The append-only journal is read in the DecisionStore notification path and corruption fails subsequent lookups.
verdicts.limitations: O(journal) cost should be measured over actual journal size; one corrupt line is a conditional hard stop.

verdicts.evidence: recent_merge.ex:309-313 checks persisted content hash after decoding; hash construction uses deterministic Erlang external term format of struct-derived maps. Adding a serialized field or changing encoding can invalidate old records.
verdicts.limitations: OTP upgrade instability requires a cross-version test; new-field mismatch is deterministic unless decoder supplies backward-compatible field normalization.

verdicts.evidence: log_file.ex:115-127 removes Logger handler when debug is off; operationally actionable boot and state degradation paths log only via Logger. The default release can therefore suppress their only signal.
verdicts.limitations: Some individual conditions may surface through status or alerts; do not generalize silence beyond listed call sites.

verdicts.evidence: build_gate_hold_monitor.ex:77 onward returns {:ignore, %State{}} when disabled; GenServer init accepts bare :ignore, not a two-tuple. A documented zero-capacity opt-out therefore fails child startup.
verdicts.limitations: Conditional on the disabled configuration; the OTP return mismatch is direct.

verdicts.evidence: model_availability.ex:54 and ci_approval_store.ex use :global.trans({Module, path}, fun). In global lock protocol the second tuple element identifies the requester; all callers on one path present the same requester ID and can enter concurrently.
verdicts.limitations: A concurrent write collision is required for data loss; verify with a controlled two-process lock test before changing lock design.

verdicts.evidence: ci_approval_store.ex:67-88 saves all sections from a supplied map without lock/re-read; journal_base_repair at 90-128 performs a separate locked update. A later stale save can erase a persisted repairing marker.
verdicts.limitations: Requires concurrency or stale caller state; actual repair volume not measured.

verdicts.evidence: executor_wake_inbox.ex:100-132 replays strict journal on init and fails child startup on corruption; flush_pending at 275 onward retries append without surfacing corruption. One bad line can prevent boot/recovery.
verdicts.limitations: Corrupt line is prerequisite; no prevalence census or recovery probe is supplied.

verdicts.evidence: executor_wake_inbox.ex:23-24 uses default 5-second enqueue call, while acknowledge_as at 58-71 holds the same GenServer through a claims lock potentially near that budget. Listener catches enqueue timeout and logs, losing a wake until replay.
verdicts.limitations: Requires overlapping slow acknowledgement and wake delivery; executor-topic replay differs from other topics.

verdicts.evidence: agent_resource_guard.ex:18 ticks every second and recursively collects children at 66-71; AgentProcessLog separately samples ps. Independent observers duplicate host process walks.
verdicts.limitations: The cited hundreds-of-processes-per-second rate is a hypothetical workload, not a measured baseline or saving claim.

verdicts.evidence: config.ex is 1,462 lines and imports BuildGate and other runtime modules; accessors mix settings reads with filesystem preparation. This is a genuine cohesion and ownership problem.
verdicts.limitations: The 114-public-function and 147-dependent-file counts were not independently reproduced; architectural severity P2.

verdicts.evidence: coding_agent.ex:81-268 returns backend runtime adapters alongside presentation, price and telemetry data; it imports Config while Config also reaches CodingAgent. This creates package extraction cycles.
verdicts.limitations: No direct P1 runtime defect follows from registry breadth alone.

verdicts.evidence: coding_agent.ex:39 and 1145 onward parse any complexity integer and take maximum, while BuildOrder and dashboard use narrower/first-label rules. The same ticket can display and route differently.
verdicts.limitations: Multiple/invalid complexity labels are prerequisite; current ticket population is unknown.

verdicts.evidence: aiur.ex:112-116 starts a flat :rest_for_one supervisor; early child failure restarts all later children, and start/2 performs host effects before supervisor. The cascade is inherent in the topology.
verdicts.limitations: Whether the topology is excessive depends on child dependencies and real failure behavior; broad risk without incident evidence remains P2.

verdicts.evidence: repo_base.ex:413-420 retains any error phase on dispatch refresh; default poll_seconds=0 and no production refresh_async caller leave the prewarm path latched until restart or manual trigger.
verdicts.limitations: Requires a prewarm failure under default polling; whether dispatch can still use an older base depends on failure phase.

verdicts.evidence: alert_ledger.ex caps at 8 MiB and compacts when an append would overflow; compaction fills near the cap with retained history and performs a full read/decode/fsync rewrite under the append lock.
verdicts.limitations: Steady-state every-append compaction depends on retained active/history sizes and entry size; no live latency or alert-drop count was measured.

verdicts.evidence: workflow_store.ex:279-285 retains old state on reload error; 302-311 logs it only. log_file.ex removes the default handler without debug, so a rejected config edit has no operator-facing notification.
verdicts.limitations: Initial config load may fail visibly; this finding concerns reload after a previously valid workflow.

verdicts.evidence: issue_log.ex:535-543 promises async record_event; writer_for_path at 616-620 calls writer_path synchronously per event. A timeout maps to no writer, so the marker is skipped although record_event returns :ok.
verdicts.limitations: Requires a busy per-ticket writer; event payload may remain in another durable source, so do not call this total event loss.

verdicts.evidence: process_reaper.ex:295-305 kills comm-guarded PIDs only if cmdline_guard permits; 323-333 treats unreadable /proc as gone. On Darwin, /proc is normally absent, so this layer skips those PIDs.
verdicts.limitations: Other backend and launcher reapers may still clean children; the claim is about this correctness-critical layer, not guaranteed orphan survival.

verdicts.evidence: test_reset.ex:582 onward derives <workspace_root>/<id>, while Workspace.Layout uses repository/project segments. A reset can report success while leaving the actual nested ticket worktree.
verdicts.limitations: Configuration whose root already includes the segment may avoid the mismatch; standard GitHub layout is affected.

verdicts.evidence: analytics_cli.ex:5 imports AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter analytics modules and uses ScopeResolver at 69-72; Alerts/RecentMergeStore likewise reference web PubSub. This inverts proposed core/web package direction.
verdicts.limitations: Architectural extraction constraint, not P1 runtime failure.

verdicts.evidence: decision_dispatch.ex:19-20 imports Orchestrator.OperatorMessages and defaults to its send function at 36-40; OperatorMessages records outcomes back in DecisionStore. The runtime dependency cycle is real.
verdicts.limitations: The source does not show a P1 defect; adapters/injection may break the cycle during extraction.

verdicts.evidence: repo_base.ex:58 onward exports common path helpers while 258 onward starts prewarm GenServer; later sections perform migration and ledger transfer. Multiple change reasons share one 1,539-line module.
verdicts.limitations: The claimed 18 dependent modules were not independently counted; this is maintainability/packaging debt.

verdicts.evidence: aiur-engine.sh:3520-3528 loops over every aiur-*-agents pidfile in the shared runtime root and reaps each, without instance-key filtering. Stopping one instance can terminate live agents owned by another.
verdicts.limitations: Requires two concurrent instances under the same runtime root; PID comm guard prevents reuse mistakes, not cross-instance killing.

verdicts.evidence: aiur-engine.sh:415-418 writes argv as newline-delimited records; CLI splits on newline and rejects empty strings. Multiline bodies and empty arguments cannot round-trip.
verdicts.limitations: Affected commands need arguments containing newline or empty text; an alternative direct RPC path may avoid it.

verdicts.evidence: The shipped share/aiur.tmux.conf contains the brittle Ctrl+C helper expansion and differs from the test harness copy; the engine resolves the shipped file. Tests of the other copy cannot validate production binding.
verdicts.limitations: A live tmux keypress reproduction is needed to confirm exact fallback on installed tmux versions.

verdicts.evidence: aiur-engine.sh:3987 onward dispatches commands from a separate list than usage and shim/npm classification. Listed omissions show documentation and build-selection drift.
verdicts.limitations: Six-list count and all runtime effects were not independently exercised; maintainability/UX severity P2.

verdicts.evidence: aiur-engine.sh is 4,179 lines and combines shell command parsing, daemon launch, tmux, process cleanup, distribution identity and upgrade logic. run_session is a large multipurpose function.
verdicts.limitations: Large script is a refactor candidate; length alone does not establish a P1 defect.

verdicts.evidence: aiur-engine.sh:2525 onward validates control arguments and emits Elixir RPC source while corresponding CLI modules validate decoded requests. The two surfaces duplicate command schemas.
verdicts.limitations: The exact 28/107/11 static counts need reproduction; no single behavioral failure is established by duplication alone.

verdicts.evidence: Launcher project-root discovery walks parents while Workflow config discovery checks cwd then user home. Starting from a nested directory can name one instance but load a different configuration.
verdicts.limitations: Requires invocation below the project root; typical root invocation is unaffected.

verdicts.evidence: resolve-version.mjs:71-77 makes nightly suffix a SHA. Lexicographic or SemVer comparison of SHA is unrelated to publication order, so same-base nightlies can be misordered.
verdicts.limitations: This is a release-channel upgrade defect; impact depends on installed nightly and comparison path, below P1 for daemon refactor priority.

verdicts.evidence: analytics/reduce.py declares the same dataset contract as RunTelemetry.Dataset and implements parallel reducers; daemon materialization refers to checkout-local script discovery.
verdicts.limitations: Need a direct outside-checkout execution before asserting universal no-op; duplication is architectural.

verdicts.evidence: IssueSync terminal pending wrapper lacks the joinable TrackerIdentity guard present in sibling wrappers; nil or unjoinable identities can be retained/re-fetched by the terminal verification path.
verdicts.limitations: P0 is overstated without prevalence or fleet-wide failure; conditional per-ticket retry churn is P1.

verdicts.evidence: Dispatcher and IssueSync repeat lifetime-latch configuration checks, including one active-trip path that reinterprets persisted state against current config.
verdicts.limitations: Potential stale semantics need a state-transition test; duplication alone is P2.

verdicts.evidence: AlertTopic keys attention until a matching resolved topic appears; cited needs_attention producers have no corresponding explicit resolver in source search. Some attentions can remain active indefinitely.
verdicts.limitations: Intentional durable attention may require human acknowledgement rather than automatic resolution; cannot call every unmatched producer a bug.

verdicts.evidence: CommentWake deactivated-entry path logs failures rather than scheduling the retry used for active/idle trusted feedback. A transient read failure can drop one review wake.
verdicts.limitations: The poller may later rediscover the comment; permanent feedback loss depends on cursor/dedup state.

verdicts.evidence: dispatcher.ex:2520 onward builds a wide untyped running map and other modules add keys ad hoc. The type boundary is weak and has produced missing-key hazards elsewhere.
verdicts.limitations: Exact 33-reader/16-writer counts not reproduced; map width itself is not P1.

verdicts.evidence: CommentWake defaults to Orchestrator facade functions at several points even though the facade delegates to siblings. This creates internal package dependency cycles.
verdicts.limitations: A call cycle in the dependency graph is not necessarily a runtime recursion; extraction concern P2.

verdicts.evidence: Dispatcher.run_poll_cycle at 53 onward combines scheduling, admission, CI probe, retry and latch policy across 2,670 lines. Multiple change reasons share a hot-path module.
verdicts.limitations: Module size and responsibility count are planning evidence, not P1 incident evidence.

verdicts.evidence: IssueSync spans 2,295 lines across terminal verification, label healing, alerts and dependency changes; cited source sections support broad responsibility split.
verdicts.limitations: Treat LOC as reorganization scope, not removable LOC or P1 failure.

verdicts.evidence: Several Orchestrator alert producers hand-roll debounce and active/resolved state with divergent lists. Reuse could reduce policy drift.
verdicts.limitations: Ten-copy count and behavioral divergence need targeted state tests; architecture severity P2.

verdicts.evidence: AgentQueueStore appends items without deletion while OperatorMessages.reject_already_queued_events scans historical digest items at enqueue. Both memory and enqueue work grow with daemon lifetime.
verdicts.limitations: Growth rate and actual daemon uptime population were not measured; this is a structural unboundedness finding.

verdicts.evidence: status_report.ex:200-236 constructs a projected State by allow-list, but subsequent status renderers access omitted fields and receive struct defaults. User-facing counters can be falsely zero.
verdicts.limitations: The raw P0 grade is high for reporting errors; confirm each omitted field against renderer access before final list.

verdicts.evidence: rate-limit fallback safety entry omits started_at; token_accounting.ex:179-183 directly accesses running_entry.started_at during teardown. A parked entry can therefore raise KeyError in the Orchestrator.
verdicts.limitations: Requires a failed replacement that retains parked entry and later teardown; direct missing-key path is credible.

verdicts.evidence: pause_resume.ex:1005 onward clears paused_reason only for enumerated cases, leaving other reasons on a resumed working entry. Status can retain a stale cause.
verdicts.limitations: Consequences are attribution/display unless another policy consumes stale reason; P1 not shown.

verdicts.evidence: PauseResume defines reason-specific lists such as input_pause_reasons at 35-40, while other lifecycle/renderers maintain separate sets. The observed omitted reason in orch-b-03 shows drift.
verdicts.limitations: Central taxonomy is a design remedy, not a P1 failure on its own.

verdicts.evidence: pause_resume.ex:2438 onward distinguishes unavailable server from failed live call; other control wrappers reportedly collapse exits. The resulting diagnostic can mislead an operator.
verdicts.limitations: Seven-copy count and each exit shape require full caller audit; no service outage follows solely from mislabeling.

verdicts.evidence: retry_engine.ex:1056 onward enumerates local budget hold shapes, while other Orchestrator consumers repeat subsets. Error routing may diverge across recovery paths.
verdicts.limitations: Need specific reachable producer/consumer mismatch before retaining P1 severity.

verdicts.evidence: RetryEngine claim release on agent retry exhaustion funnels through tracker-specific reason/text. Operators can see the wrong cause.
verdicts.limitations: Misclassification is real but no P1 operational consequence demonstrated.

verdicts.evidence: rate_limit_fallback.ex:34-36 limits one transition per tick; failed label writes count toward that limit while entries are sorted. A persistently failing first ticket can starve all later fallback/revert transitions.
verdicts.limitations: Requires repeatable label failure on the first eligible ticket; no observed fleet instance supplied.

verdicts.evidence: push_routing.ex:543 onward drains pending auto-resume on each tick and retains hints after any error without distinguishing capacity from non-capacity refusal. A permanent refusal can spin durable control attempts.
verdicts.limitations: Actual request rate is bounded by reconcile cadence; repeated persistence should be reproduced for each refusal class.

verdicts.evidence: RateLimitFallback.redispatch at 427 onward retains a parked lifecycle-fenced entry on failed replacement, while other backend-swap paths have independent teardown/re-admit logic. The safety contract is not shared.
verdicts.limitations: Specific failure in each alternative flow needs mutation/state tests; duplication alone would be P2.

verdicts.evidence: reconciler.ex:29-36 calls the Orchestrator facade for sibling work, while facade delegates back to submodules. Dependency direction complicates extraction.
verdicts.limitations: Architectural cycle, not a demonstrated runtime recursion or P1 failure.

verdicts.evidence: orchestrator/state.ex:15 onward defines a roughly 100-field state struct while running entries remain wide maps. Field/type drift is plausible and missing-key defect has a concrete example in orch-b-02.
verdicts.limitations: The struct size itself is not P1; exact 16-writer count not independently reproduced.

verdicts.evidence: TokenAccounting handles streamed Codex updates inside Orchestrator and calls StatusReport dashboard notification for each; projection copies state and broadcasts. Work scales with update rate and fleet size.
verdicts.limitations: No measured CPU or mailbox delay is provided, so inherited P1 performance severity is unverified.

verdicts.evidence: status_report.ex:716-723 maps unavailable decision count to {0, :unavailable}; downstream waiting classifiers consume the 0 and can mark a still-waiting ticket resolved.
verdicts.limitations: Requires DecisionStore/SubscriptionStore unavailability; health bit exists but is not used in the classifier.

verdicts.evidence: config/schema/agent.ex:185-191 declares max_consecutive_noop_turns, but explicit cast list at 277-323 omits it. Ecto ignores operator-supplied values and the default always wins.
verdicts.limitations: P0 is overstated for a ignored safety tuning key absent demonstrated runaway turn; config behavior is deterministic.

verdicts.evidence: schema.ex:72-80 normalizes and casts maps, while embedded changesets use permitted fields without unknown-key validation. Misspelled settings can be accepted with defaults, as platform-misc-01 demonstrates.
verdicts.limitations: Some obsolete keys receive explicit rejection; the claim must distinguish those from generally silent unknown keys.

verdicts.evidence: guardian.ex:383-390 loops in :reaping with nil provider and provider_expected true; release at 186-191 re-enters that path. Persisted phase can survive restart without a timer to resolve it.
verdicts.limitations: Requires owner death before provider identity is tracked or remote cleanup shape; manual receipt removal may recover but is unsafe.

verdicts.evidence: workspace/ownership/store.ex:292-299 performs fsync atomic write then sync_fun on each persist; default sync_fun is Fs.sync_filesystem at 97-104. All lease transitions serialize through the Store GenServer.
verdicts.limitations: Host-wide sync latency and actual transition rate were not measured; the 5-second timeout risk is conditional.

verdicts.evidence: workspace/reconstruction.ex:24-29 holds with_log_lock across prepare hook; 48 onward implements global spin acquisition. Event/alert writes for same workspace take this lock, so long hook stalls publication.
verdicts.limitations: Claimed ten-minute block is a configured timeout upper bound, not observed latency.

verdicts.evidence: workspace/hooks.ex:125-132 runs shell in a Task; timeout kills the BEAM Task, not necessarily shell descendants. remote.ex:35-43 similarly brutal-kills task without remote process cancellation.
verdicts.limitations: Whether a specific shell/SSH child survives Port closure depends on process topology; test with a child that ignores SIGHUP before quantifying.

verdicts.evidence: host_lock.ex:178-181 uses exclusive create; conflict recovery reads stale holder and removes path without comparing the inode/content before deletion. Two reclaimers can remove one another's newly created lock.
verdicts.limitations: Requires two contenders and a stale holder; PID reuse is a separate conditional liveness defect.

verdicts.evidence: logs/retention.ex:102-132 sorts all shared session directories and excludes only current from deletion. Another live daemon's older directory can be removed under cap pressure.
verdicts.limitations: Requires multiple live daemons sharing log root and cap pressure; deletion of open-file data varies by OS semantics.

verdicts.evidence: current_run_membership/store/runtime.ex:150-154 sets writable?: false on append error; store.ex:98-105 refuses future observations. A transient I/O error can latch terminal membership updates for the run.
verdicts.limitations: Persistent corruption marker may warrant continued fail-closed behavior; recovery should distinguish transient from integrity failure.

verdicts.evidence: dispatch_policy.ex:1079-1082 normalizes trim/downcase while other tracker and summary modules use different slug substitutions. State matching can disagree at cross-boundary inputs.
verdicts.limitations: The claimed twelve sites and five semantics need a complete census; a concrete default-state misroute should be tested before P1.

verdicts.evidence: upgrade/registry.ex:13-15 passes timeout: to Req.get; Req 0.7 option validation does not register that name, so fetch returns rescued error and suppresses notice.
verdicts.limitations: Needs a dependency-version-specific execution check; impact is an upgrade notice, below P1.

verdicts.evidence: current_run_projections.ex:163 subscribes to AiurWeb.ObservabilityPubSub, and its state.ex:9 imports web UnitsRow. Core current-run projections depend on the web namespace.
verdicts.limitations: Architectural extraction constraint, not P1 runtime failure.

verdicts.evidence: usage_ledger/counter_policy.ex:8-11 retains idempotency MapSet and dump at 43-46 serializes all keys; capacity eventually refuses appends while raw compaction does not prune policy.
verdicts.limitations: P0 severity requires evidence of approach to 50,000 keys or 1 MiB in current runs; permanent latch is conditional on volume.

verdicts.evidence: normalizer.ex:18-23 runs every registered adapter; Codex ThreadUsage and TurnUsage extract absolute and delta views of the same token payload. Aggregate queries sum both relationship streams.
verdicts.limitations: Double counting depends on both envelopes being accepted for the same payload; a fixture-level end-to-end aggregate test should pin the exact factor.

verdicts.evidence: price_table/data.ex:19-21 and 40-42 tag price rows with relationship revisions that differ from headless adapter revisions; exact lookup cannot price those cells. Required tiers also lack partition propagation.
verdicts.limitations: Impact is absent API-equivalent estimate, not real billing; price-table/config version may change later.

verdicts.evidence: usage_aggregate/store.ex:67-69 catches up only on ledger-delta messages; subscription happens in bootstrap at 73 onward, while restarted ledger Store loses in-memory subscribers. Aggregate can remain stale indefinitely.
verdicts.limitations: Requires isolated ledger child restart while aggregate remains alive; top-level rest_for_one restart may recreate both in other failure paths.

verdicts.evidence: usage_compaction/coordinator.ex:153-154 skips cycles whenever health != :ok; retire/finalize failures at 217-224 call halt. No in-process retry clears degraded health.
verdicts.limitations: Requires transient error; destructive-phase manifest implications depend on where failure happens.

verdicts.evidence: headless/emitter.ex:20-28 returns outcome with coverage facts but only publishes envelopes; 64 onward launches append task whose result is not propagated. Source drift or ledger append failure can silently stop accounting.
verdicts.limitations: Actual protocol drift and append-failure occurrence are unknown; this is observability and accounting coverage risk.

verdicts.evidence: run_telemetry/dataset.ex:146-154 merge dedupes only by record_id, while build at 601 onward also dedupes lifecycle event keys; Python reducer is a third rule set. Equivalent records can reduce differently.
verdicts.limitations: Need a shared fixture proving a user-visible discrepancy before P1; duplication itself is P2.

verdicts.evidence: usage_aggregate/key.ex:17-19 evaluates CodingAgent provider/backends at compile time; CodingAgent registry references usage and meter modules in return. Proposed packages have compile and runtime cycles.
verdicts.limitations: Architectural dependency finding, not direct P1 operation.

verdicts.evidence: provider_account_generation/continuity.ex:21-25 updates session binding state on each retain; Context at 12-17 uses process dictionary. Mutable global/process-local state complicates package ownership.
verdicts.limitations: Persistent-term churn cost was not measured; do not claim fleet performance regression from source alone.

verdicts.evidence: test_reset_test.exs:153-179 creates a fixture inside shared System.tmp_dir!/aiur-workspaces but cleanup recursively removes the parent. A sibling process's workspace can be deleted.
verdicts.limitations: Requires a concurrent workspace under that shared parent; ExUnit seriality within one VM does not protect other processes.

verdicts.evidence: Named Orchestrator defaults to an immediate poll; TestSupport default Linear workflow points at api.linear.app. Tests starting it without poll disable or request fake can make real HTTPS calls.
verdicts.limitations: About-44 count needs rerun of start-link census; network restrictions may cause quick failures rather than long waits.

verdicts.evidence: orchestrator_status_test.exs is 4,880 lines and tests status, workspace cleanup, queue, CI, telemetry and pause paths in one module.
verdicts.limitations: Large heterogeneous test file slows ownership/refactor work but is not a P1 defect.

verdicts.evidence: workspace_and_config_test.exs is 3,640 lines and imports workspace, config, tracker and dispatch modules in one suite.
verdicts.limitations: Line count and test count are review navigation facts, not P1 risk.

verdicts.evidence: This unit rewrites WorkflowStore files and application-supervised singleton state to configure tests; package tests therefore inherit global app setup.
verdicts.limitations: The universal claim no package can be tested independently is too broad; pure modules already have isolated tests. P2 architecture concern.

verdicts.evidence: read_cache_test.exs:826-834 directly deletes live named ETS tables and stops their owner while the application rest_for_one supervisor is running. Restart can affect later children and cases.
verdicts.limitations: Exact restart count depends on supervisor order and concurrent test scheduling.

verdicts.evidence: view_state_sweep_test.exs:509-514 records delivery on the global ModeRegistry for owner/repo and does not restore it; cache TTL tests reuse owner/repo. Cross-test state can alter expected cache freshness.
verdicts.limitations: Order-dependent failure requires affected reader tests run afterward in same VM.

verdicts.evidence: read_cache_test.exs:41 onward maintains its own readiness polling and temporary fallback, unlike shared TestSupport recovery. A test-owned named cache can disappear at case teardown.
verdicts.limitations: The fallback must actually execute for the failure; class as P2 until recurrence demonstrated.

verdicts.evidence: github/transport.ex:79-92 returns literal test-gh-token when request_fun option is present and token absent, in production code.
verdicts.limitations: Raw review itself found no production caller taking this combination today; latent seam merits removal but not P1.

verdicts.evidence: issues_test.exs:20-28 manually saves/erases global token cache and environment, while other GitHub suites have differing setup. Duplicated global fixtures invite order dependence.
verdicts.limitations: The 22-file/three-variant count was not recounted; no one reproducible failure follows from the pattern alone.

verdicts.evidence: Architecture tests read production files through hard-coded lib-relative paths or scan only current package. A package carve can silently narrow the source scanned.
verdicts.limitations: The carve has not happened; migrate tests with changed ownership, not as an emergency P1 fix.

verdicts.evidence: self_pause_answer_test.exs:10 onward captures live Orchestrator state, cancels its tick, then restores stale timer refs in on_exit. Restoring a reference cannot restore a cancelled timer message.
verdicts.limitations: A later wake path might reschedule in some cases; test suite order and singleton lifetime determine impact.

verdicts.evidence: dispatcher_test.exs:63-91 reads/writes many :aiur application env test seams. Shared VM globals can leak across async processes and require hand restoration.
verdicts.limitations: The 41/40/197 census needs reproducible script; no individual failing interleaving demonstrated here.

verdicts.evidence: TestSupport.__using__ at 228 onward imposes broad global setup and aliases on all users, including pure tests. Splitting helpers would reduce fixture work.
verdicts.limitations: The exact 37-user/four-unneeded count should be checked before using as LOC or speed claim.

verdicts.evidence: session_lifecycle_test.exs:934-941 registers literal OS pid 424242 through real guardian paths. If that PID belongs to an unrelated live process when the test runs, identity capture and cleanup may signal it.
verdicts.limitations: PID coincidence is unlikely but avoidable; use a controlled child PID or injectable killer to eliminate host risk.

verdicts.evidence: Several tests assert production source strings and repo-relative paths; moving files in the carve will break or narrow these checks.
verdicts.limitations: The 24-file/43-test count was not independently reproduced; refactor migration concern, not P1 runtime defect.

verdicts.evidence: This unit calls :sys.replace_state on named application processes and restarts Aiur.Supervisor children. Global mutable fixture state can leak into unrelated tests.
verdicts.limitations: The cited 117-site count is unverified; specific contamination depends on test ordering and cleanup.

verdicts.evidence: TestSupport.reset_global_state! at 207-215 ignores ensure_resource_store_running result then calls ResourceStore.reset, which is a no-op if missing. Setup can appear successful while global state is absent.
verdicts.limitations: Requires a failed child recovery; later failure attribution is the primary cost.

verdicts.evidence: TestSupport.__using__ expands use ExUnit.Case without forwarding opts; all users become synchronous and inherit the full 1,663-line global fixture.
verdicts.limitations: The 194-user count was not independently recounted; synchronous suite cost needs timing to rank above P2.

verdicts.evidence: graph_projection_test.exs:14-19 starts named Aiur.PubSub under a temporary ExUnit supervisor if absent. That process dies with the test/module, leaving later tests without the shared bus.
verdicts.limitations: Only triggers when the application child is absent; count of 17 sites requires census.

verdicts.evidence: Core CurrentRunSummary and multiple CLI surfaces import AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter policy and presenter modules. Proposed web package split would require moving the domain rules or introducing a lower shared boundary.
verdicts.limitations: Architectural inversion, not a P1 runtime failure; claimed five CLIs should be counted in final synthesis.

verdicts.evidence: units_control_policy.ex:273 onward defines paused/queued predicates separately from UnitsPolicy and FleetFilters. Divergent conditions can display mismatched filters and control buttons.
verdicts.limitations: Need a single reachable row fixture and observed UI divergence before calling P1.

verdicts.evidence: Ticket search shares an eight-term limit between query parser and indexed title/body words; words after the eighth unique term cannot match.
verdicts.limitations: Scoped to Tickets panel search; source defect is clear but P1 priority is high without usage impact.

verdicts.evidence: decision_card.ex:92-98 renders a DecisionAction for dismissed decisions, while DecisionCommands selected-open guard excludes dismissed selected decision. The offered Change choice action returns a misleading not-loaded error.
verdicts.limitations: Requires a selected dismissed Command; no durable write occurs, but direct UI affordance is broken.

verdicts.evidence: DecisionCommands safe wrappers collapse GenServer call exits, including ambiguous timeouts, into store_unavailable and put_error discards idempotency key. A committed-but-unanswered write can be retried under a new key.
verdicts.limitations: Duplicate action outcome depends on server completion after caller timeout and action semantics; needs a timeout fixture.

verdicts.evidence: decision_presenter.ex:20-27 rescues/catches any presentation error and returns [], so a retained blocking Command can vanish from the list while counts still include it. This is stronger evidence than a blanket rescue count.
verdicts.limitations: The 46/zero logging census was not rerun; final finding should cite concrete disappearance path, not just style.

verdicts.evidence: analytics/charts.ex:113-121 unconditionally uses model.cap for a drawn cap line. The model falls back to local config/default 10 when effective cap is unknown, while other labels acknowledge unknown.
verdicts.limitations: Requires unavailable effective cap; line is visual inference, not a measured capacity.

verdicts.evidence: streamdeck_channel.ex:78-90 and 107-113 execute pause/resume/implement for authenticated deck socket without checking observability.dashboard_writable, while router and emulator enforce the read-only setting.
verdicts.limitations: Authentication still applies; this is a policy bypass for an already-authorized device, not an unauthenticated external write.

verdicts.evidence: control_center_cache.ex:27-35 uses infinite GenServer.call and executes provided loaders inside the one cache server; aiur.ex:115 uses rest_for_one. Slow or crashing presentation blocks clients or cascades later children.
verdicts.limitations: Need actual loader duration and supervisor ordering to quantify blast radius; structural risk is clear.

verdicts.evidence: StreamdeckProjection and RunSummaryStrip copy durable meter mapping with a single-clause Enum.map guard; ModelAvailability can persist reset/window without a nonzero percent. The reader then raises FunctionClauseError on an accepted record.
verdicts.limitations: Requires a sparse provider bucket or zero limit; source shape should be fixture-tested across both surfaces.

verdicts.evidence: dashboard_live.ex is 2,858 lines and handles decisions, units, tickets, drawers, controls and multiple subscriptions in one LiveView. Responsibility split is supported by source.
verdicts.limitations: Module size is a maintainability concern; no P1 runtime defect follows from length.

verdicts.evidence: AiurWeb.ObservabilityPubSub defines a domain update topic consumed/published by Aiur.* modules; BuildOrderPresenter is called from core CLI. This inverts the proposed web package boundary.
verdicts.limitations: Architectural issue only; overlaps web-occ-01 and loose-3-07 for deduplication.

verdicts.evidence: streamdeck_key_face_contract.ex:142-185 embeds JSON by fixed relative path into packages/streamdeck at compile time; moving the sidecar independently would break Elixir compilation.
verdicts.limitations: Current monorepo includes the file, so this is an extraction constraint, not current P1 failure.

verdicts.evidence: observability_api_controller.ex:245 onward maps control error atoms to HTTP classes independently of agent_control_cli.ex:3355 onward. Some user conflicts fall into generic 503.
verdicts.limitations: Mislabelled HTTP status can affect clients, but no P1 outage or security consequence is demonstrated.

verdicts.evidence: decision_api_controller.ex broad rescue converts unexpected exceptions to 503 with no log; other web paths also catch and return stale socket/state. This can hide functional bugs and misstate cause.
verdicts.limitations: The 83 rescue/2 Logger aggregate was not independently reproduced; report concrete call sites rather than treating all catches as faults.

verdicts.evidence: presenter.ex:543-547 falls back to <workspace.root>/<identifier>; workspace/layout.ex:33-47 inserts a repo segment and sanitizes identity when configured. Idle issue API can advertise a non-existent path.
verdicts.limitations: Running/retry rows with an actual workspace path are unaffected; CLI consumers of idle path should be checked for impact.
